endorsements.quote: Clear governance should be established alongside any clinical validation, addressing data protection, auditable decision logs, human oversight, and defined lines of responsibility.

Prospective studies with authentic emergency-call data are required to evaluate sensitivity, missed OHCA (false negatives), false-positive activation, processing latency, language variation, and performance relative to trained dispatchers.
The integrated system should also include fail-safe design and operational redundancy, so that failure of any single component does not interrupt the chain of survival.

If AI analysis is unavailable or uncertain, conventional dispatcher protocols should remain the default.
AI outputs should support, not replace, dispatcher assessment and decision-making.

Additional safeguards should include real-time system-health checks, predefined mission-abort thresholds, safe-landing procedures, adequate battery reserve, manual override, cybersecurity protection, and auditable event logs.
Emergency departments and public-health programs should deliver CPR and AED training that includes drone-delivery scenarios.
Implementation should, however, remain guided by rigorous prospective validation focused on patient outcomes and equitable access.

unlisted_practices: Conduct platform-, payload-, and site-specific weather risk assessments before routine deployment of drone-delivered AED programs.
Keep ground-based EMS pathways available whenever weather exceeds the approved drone operating envelope or prevents safe mission completion.
Set explicit performance thresholds for false-positive and missed-OHCA errors in AI-supported dispatch before deployment.
Address data-privacy obligations for analysis of caller audio, video, and location data in AI-supported dispatch.
Implement cybersecurity protections against interception, spoofing, and unauthorized activation of drone launch commands and mission data.
Proceed with ground EMS dispatch and dispatcher-assisted CPR independently of AI confidence, drone availability, weather, or network connectivity.
Maintain ground response and activate nearby fixed AEDs or community first responders when a drone cannot launch, loses communication, or fails to deliver.
Specify communication systems by functional requirements (reliability, latency, concurrency) and degrade progressively from 5G to other cellular, voice, or text channels.
Delay large-scale integration of ultraportable AEDs into drone delivery until regulatory authorization and clinical evidence show comparable defibrillation performance and safety.
Evaluate equity in drone and community first responder coverage by geography, socioeconomic conditions, digital access, language, age, and community response capacity.

Guide equity-oriented deployment of drone-delivered AED systems by local OHCA incidence, EMS response times, existing AED coverage, connectivity, socioeconomic conditions, and community response capacity.
Use dispatch protocols that separate CPR, drone retrieval, and AED operation tasks, dispatching community responders to intercept the drone so the bystander can continue compressions.
Prospectively evaluate augmented-reality navigation for locating drones or delivered AEDs before routine implementation.

Evaluate the entire clinical and operational pathway in future studies, including mission completion, device retrieval, CPR interruptions, time to pad attachment, and time to first shock, rather than AED arrival time alone.
Perform dedicated local cost-effectiveness modeling for low-resource settings rather than extrapolating a single high-income estimate.
Provide targeted responder recruitment and training in underserved communities, publicly funded responder programs, and multilingual accessible alert interfaces.
Combine legal-liability protections such as Good Samaritan laws with technological support and community mobilization.
